Prefer cuts placed after the completed predicate or after clause‑final particles; attach closing punctuation or quotes to the piece that contains the predicate so the left fragment is not left dangling or unentailed.

- Consider left‑headed modifiers (long pre‑nominal relative or adjectival phrases): avoid separating a modifier from its head noun, since that breaks attachment and reference. That said, do not preserve multi‑token names or transliterations if keeping them whole would isolate punctuation, reporting verbs, or core predicates; in such cases prefer a cut that keeps the clause predicate and its punctuation/verb intact, even if the name is split.

A useful cut point is after a completed predicate (including its aspectual marker) and, when present, with the predicate's trailing punctuation or closing particle attached.

- When a multi‑token name, transliteration, or technical term crosses a marker, do not preserve the name at the cost of isolating punctuation, a reporting verb/quote/colon, or a short predicate fragment. Prefer a cut that keeps the clause predicate and its attached punctuation/closing marks intact, even if the name must be split; ensure punctuation stays with the unit it punctuates.
